nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is the VX-07 ARES armour.
@image2 is Marcus.
@image3 gives the architecture, wet asphalt, overcast rain light and parked traffic only; its calmly walking pedestrians and moving traffic are replaced by the panicking crowd and abandoned cars described below.
@image4 is the monster, standing three times Marcus's height. The smaller figure beside it in that reference is a scale comparison only and does not appear in the video.

summary:
[reference generation] @image2 armours up, takes a thrown car head-on, punches @image4 and sends it down the street.

detailed_description:
Blockbuster superhero film, photoreal, overcast rain, wet asphalt, deep street perspective under the elevated track of @image3. Every pedestrian runs away from the fight for the whole video; nobody walks, nobody watches calmly.

[Shot 1] Close-up on @image2 in the flooded street in his tuxedo. Plates of @image1 come in fast from off frame and build onto him, running continuously across the whole shot, never rushing and never springing back: every piece travels inward and seats with weight, cyan seams lighting as each lock closes. Nothing detaches or floats free. People stream past behind him, running the other way. His lips stay pressed closed and he does not speak at any point in the video.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, cut low and wide as @image4 tears an empty parked taxi off the road and hurls it down the lane, the car turning end over end. The camera Trucks backwards with large amplitude at fast speed.

[Shot 3] At 00:06.000, cut to a low side-on shot: @image2 stands right of frame in profile, visor, chest plate and crossed forearms square to screen-left in every frame. The taxi enters from the left edge intact and filling the frame, slams into his forearms and stops dead, crumpling around them while he is driven backwards through the water, heels gouging two long trenches before he plants. The wreck then breaks apart off his front and drops.

[Shot 4] At 00:09.000, cut in tight past @image4's shoulder onto @image2. He drops his shoulder and drives his fist across the frame into the chest plate of @image4, and the fist stays buried there for the rest of the shot, forearm plates compressing, @image4's chest caving around it. @image4 stays on its feet and in place throughout this shot; nothing leaves the ground yet. The camera is Static.

[Shot 5] At 00:10.600, cut wide down the street as @image4 flies ten metres backwards through the air, lands hard and skids through the water. A low sheet of white spray rolls outward along the street with it, hiding the parked cars as it passes. The camera is Static. Both helmets stay sealed and neither character speaks.

overall_soundscape:
Hard rain on metal and asphalt and an elevated train rumbling overhead through the whole video. Running footsteps splashing away and a distant wordless crowd cry, never fully stopping. Tearing sheet metal and a long rising whoosh as the car comes down the lane, then one huge dull impact of mass on mass, metal buckling, heels grinding through grit, glass cascading off him. The punch is one enormous low boom with a hard metallic crack inside it and a half-second of near-silence behind it, then the rip of spray, a heavy body hitting water and sliding, car alarms down the block and armour ticking and draining. Nobody in the video speaks any words.

non_diegetic_music:
Low taiko building under the armour build. Distorted low brass enters on the throw and drops out completely half a beat before the fist lands, then one sustained chord over the landing with the drums returning underneath.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is the yellow robot.
@image2 is the yellow car. Use its shape, paint and black stripes only; the studio backdrop and the multiple views in that sheet are a reference layout and do not appear in the video.
@image3 is the abandoned brick factory yard, and gives the architecture, the gantry crane, the scrap piles, the dirt ground and the low sunset light.
@image4 is the grey monster, standing a head taller than @image1. The smaller figure beside it in that reference is a scale comparison only and does not appear in the video.
@image1 and @image2 are the same character in two forms, never two separate things in frame.

summary:
[reference generation] @image2 slides into the yard, transforms into @image1, trades blows with @image4 and rockets it.

detailed_description:
Blockbuster action film in the style of a live-action Transformers movie, photoreal, handheld shoulder-mounted camera with constant human float in every shot, low sunset light, dust hanging across the yard of @image3.

[Shot 1] Wide low angle across the dirt. @image2 comes in fast from the left edge, brakes hard and slides broadside toward the lens, rear wheels spinning, throwing a sheet of dust that rolls outward across the yard and keeps travelling rather than settling.

[Shot 2] At 00:02.600, cut closer as @image2 transforms into @image1 epic transformers movies like, every parts moves, rotates, folds, and roll. nothing left on the ground
[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, cut tight and low as @image4 charges in from screen-right and swings. @image1 blocks it on a forearm, drives a fist into the chest of @image4, then takes a backhand that snaps its head aside and puts it back two steps through the dirt. The camera is Static.

[Shot 4] At 00:09.000, cut in close on the right forearm of @image1. Plates on the forearm hinge outward and lock open, a rocket pod rotates up out of the housing on a pivot arm and seats hard, its tube aligning forward. The camera is Static.

[Shot 5] At 00:11.300, cut behind @image1 with its right arm held out large in the foreground on the left of frame, the open pod on that forearm sharp and in shot throughout, @image4 downrange. The rocket leaves that tube in frame with a hard backblast off the pod, crosses the yard on a corkscrewing smoke trail and strikes @image4 in the chest. A fireball climbs and rolls outward, throwing burning scrap, a wall of dust racing ahead of it along the ground. Bricks come down off the factory wall and stay down. Neither character speaks at any point in the video.

overall_soundscape:
Wind across an empty yard and loose metal ticking. A hard engine howl and a long gravel skid on the arrival. The transform starts as a fine dense rustle of hundreds of small plates and ratcheting gears, then deepens into heavy hydraulics and big panels seating, ending with two feet planting in dirt. Charging footfalls, a heavy forearm block, one impact boom with a metallic crack, a flat cracking backhand and boots dragging through grit. Plates hinging open and a pod locking into place. Rocket ignition and a hiss across the yard, a low detonation with a deep sub thud under it, burning scrap raining down, fire roaring, bricks collapsing. No voices anywhere in the video.

non_diegetic_music:
Low brass swell under the arrival. Percussion builds through the transform and drops out completely as the backhand lands, leaving the pod deployment almost bare. One full orchestral hit on the detonation, then a slow sustained chord over the fire.

Then charging footfalls, a forearm block, and one enormous impact boom with a metallic crack inside it. A low detonation with a deep sub thud under it, burning scrap raining across the yard, fire roaring, bricks collapsing and warped metal ticking as it cools. No voices anywhere in the video.
